title: Claim-key agreement under the revised statement key (ADR-0019)
question: Under the revised statement key (anchor segment located by its locator, plus the ordinal of the statement's first sentence in it), how close does claim-key agreement on the 70 aligned A/B pairs come to meaning-key agreement? (B3, OPEN-D3-4)
method: S0 passes A and B aligned per unit with the I-R2 instruments as code/s0d_compare.py does; keys from instruments.keys.compute_keys with each statement's anchor replaced, for keys only, by the anchor segment's locator in key form (corpus_structure.core.locators, generated on the rendition) and the first sentence's ordinal (unit inside units, details for proofs and solutions, paragraph or list item outside units; an assumption inside another statement's anchor takes that statement's part). The four S0 variants recomputed by the same driver as a check. One rendition per page, where locators and segments correspond one to one, so the figures are comparable with the S0 rows.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6*, results/s6/, records/s6.*

outputs.role: pairs whose claim keys differ, with causes

results.name: pairs_differing_only_by_statement
results.note: U6: pass B splits the paragraph into two statements (st_recall, st_cor at ordinal 2), pass A has one

results.name: pairs_differing_in_meaning_too
results.note: conditions, modality, a parameter value's latex: disagreements about the fact, which no key rule should hide

conclusion: The revised statement key raises claim-key agreement from 21 to 38 of 70 (meaning keys 41), and with the label rule from 48 to 51 against 54 meaning keys: the 3 remaining statement-caused differences are one paragraph that pass B splits into two statements. Statement identity (B3) does the work; claim keys now differ from meaning keys only where the passes disagree about statement segmentation.
